text:
Jake Sanderson logged 4:30 in Ottawa's opener on Oct. 3 and didn't play again until Oct. 21. Since then he has looked like the Senators' engine: nine assists and ten points in nine games, and a heavy workload, peaking at 29:18 in an overtime loss to Los Angeles.

He was one of the best defensemen in the league last season by Evolving-Hockey's count (3.3 wins above replacement, fifth of 215), much of it on the power play. He skates (EDGE puts his top speed in the 89th percentile) and shoots hard (92.7 mph, 81st percentile).

Our numbers are less sold on this start. Ottawa holds only 49% of the five-on-five expected goals (chance quality) with him on, about four points worse than without him, and he ranks 460th of 496 skaters in wins added. His 2.93 points per 60 sits far above our range of 1.61 to 2.30 for him. The assists are real, but they're running ahead of the play. If the five-on-five numbers come up, the points can stay. If not, expect a cooler November. We'd guess the former, given last season.
headline: Sanderson's assists outrun his five-on-five
